verdictRationale: The Writer resolved the four carried issues with concrete manifest, policy, approval, and path-safety invariants. One remaining safety-sensitive gap is that UPDATE_POLICY.md is treated as an enforceable policy input without a machine-readable contract, so implementations can diverge or accidentally auto-apply under ambiguous human prose.

falsifiability.failureCondition: A customer install has agentic-os.local.json set to stable safe_additive while UPDATE_POLICY.md contains only ambiguous prose or conflicting prose, and apply still writes a safe_additive file.
falsifiability.observableSignal: The updater reports policy consistency as ok or auto-applies an update despite no canonical parseable policy fields in UPDATE_POLICY.md.
falsifiability.measurementMethod: Create fixture roots with structured local policy plus multiple UPDATE_POLICY.md variants: missing fields, prose-only policy, conflicting channel, conflicting auto-update setting, and explicit matching fields. Run update status, doctor --json, plan, and apply against each fixture and inspect effective policy and write behavior.
falsifiability.threshold: Only UPDATE_POLICY.md files containing the required canonical machine-readable policy fields may permit customer auto-apply; all ambiguous or conflicting variants must make apply fail closed.

newIssueList.title: UPDATE_POLICY.md consistency is not machine-enforceable
newIssueList.description: The spec requires agentic-os.local.json and UPDATE_POLICY.md to agree on channel, policy mode, environment, and auto-update before customer safe_additive apply. However UPDATE_POLICY.md is described as human-readable, with no required frontmatter, canonical fields, schema, or parsing rule. Under adversarial reading, one implementation could treat prose as sufficient while another fails closed, and customer auto-update safety would depend on parser interpretation rather than a crisp invariant.
newIssueList.suggestedFix: Require UPDATE_POLICY.md to include a canonical YAML frontmatter block or embedded JSON policy block with schema_version, environment, channel, policy_mode, auto_update_enabled, executable_update_policy, and customer_approved_id fields. Define that missing, unparsable, or conflicting machine-readable fields make apply fail closed.
newIssueList.lineRef: Installed Root Files; Channels, Defaults, And Policy Precedence; Acceptance Criteria 6

ledgerReview.rationale: The manifest now has mandatory files[] entries and blocks write planning unless exactly one explicit file entry backs the operation.
Missing, invalid, unreadable, or inconsistent policy now fails closed as pinned_version for apply, and the contradictory open decision was removed.
The approval artifact is now concrete and bound to install id, root id, manifest digest, plan digest, operation ids, and expiration.
Path safety is explicit and repeated at planning and pre-write time, including containment, symlink escape denial, and local-only target restrictions.

preserveList.summary: The spec correctly makes every file write traceable to explicit manifest metadata rather than package-level version intent.
The pre-write re-gate is a strong invariant for preventing stale plans from overwriting operator edits.
Telemetry is constrained by an explicit allowlist and fail-closed behavior before sending.
